slides.title: Daily p*rn users were nearly twice as likely to say [[they feel lonely most of the time.]]
slides.sub: What a 2024 survey found — and why it matters on Day 19.

slides.title: vs [[20%]]
slides.body: An Institute for Family Studies / YouGov survey (2024) found 36% of daily p*rn users felt lonely all or most of the time — compared with 20% of people who rarely or never watch.

slides.title: It goes [[both ways]]
slides.body: Loneliness can push people toward p*rn. P*rn can pull people away from others. The survey can't say which came first — but the loop is real for many.

slides.title: Day 19 is a [[good]] time to notice
slides.body: With p*rn out of your evenings, the loneliness it was covering may feel louder. That's not failure. That's information.

slides.title: Lonely tonight? [[Try]]
items: Send one voice note instead of a text.
Go somewhere people are — even just a café.
Say yes to the next invite, however small.
Tell someone it's been a lonely week.

carousels.name: How to support someone doing NNN without becoming their babysitter

slides.title: Your partner is quitting p*rn this November. [[How to help without becoming his babysitter.]]
You're not the [[blocker]]
slides.body: Checking his phone every night turns you into the police. His recovery from p*rn is his job. Your job is the relationship.

slides.title: Ask, don't [[interrogate]]
slides.body: "How's it going this week?" beats "Did you watch p*rn today?" Open questions get honest answers.

slides.title: Celebrate [[effort]]
slides.body: Notice the small things — he's sleeping better, more present, more honest. Say it out loud. It matters more than you think.

slides.title: Protect [[yourself]] too
items: Have your own support — a friend, a counselor.
Be honest about how his p*rn use affected you.
Set boundaries you'll actually keep.
Remember his relapse isn't your failure.

carousels.name: You don't want p*rn. You want to feel nothing for a while.

slides.title: You don't really want p*rn. [[You want to feel nothing for a while.]]
slides.sub: And that's a need you can meet in better ways.

slides.title: The [[off switch]]
slides.body: After a long day, your brain wants to go quiet. P*rn shuts everything off for a few minutes. It's not desire. It's escape from feeling.

slides.title: Numb isn't [[rest]]
slides.body: Numbing doesn't recharge you. You come back to the same stress — plus guilt. Real rest leaves you better than before.

slides.title: Find a [[better]] off switch
slides.body: A hot shower. A long walk with no phone. Music with your eyes closed. Lying on the floor for ten minutes. Quiet without the crash.

slides.title: When you want to [[switch off]]
items: Say it: "I want to feel nothing right now."
Ask: what am I trying not to feel?
Pick one real off switch from the list.
Notice the p*rn urge shrink.
slides.note: What's your real off switch? Share it — someone needs the idea 👇

carousels.name: Healing or self-punishment? 7 tells during NNN

slides.title: Is No Nut November healing you from p*rn — [[or just punishing you? 7 tells.]]
slides.sub: Recovery built on self-hate usually collapses.

slides.title: Signs [[1–4]]
items: You call yourself disgusting every time you think about p*rn.
One slip means you "don't deserve" to try again.
You won't tell anyone because you're too ashamed.
You're miserable — and think that proves it's working.

slides.title: Signs [[5–7]]
items: You've stopped doing anything enjoyable "as penance."
You count days like a sentence, not progress.
You're already planning how you'll fail.

slides.title: Shame isn't [[fuel]].
slides.body: Many people in recovery say shame kept them going back to p*rn, not away from it. You can be serious about quitting and kind to yourself.

slides.title: Heal [[instead]]
items: Talk to yourself like a friend who's trying.
Add good things to your days, not just rules.
Tell one person — shame shrinks when shared.
If it gets dark, talk to a professional or a helpline.
slides.note: Recognize yourself here? Save this and come back to it 🔖

slides.title:
Heal, don't punish.
[[RezenIt is shame-free.]]
slides.lead: Shame-free progress tracking, journaling and an AI coach that treats you like a person, not a failure.

carousels.name: You're not waiting for the right moment to tell her

slides.title: "Waiting for the right moment" to tell her about p*rn? [[You're hoping she never finds out.]]
slides.sub: Be honest about which one it is.

slides.title: The right moment [[never comes]]
slides.body: Too soon. Too late. She's stressed. You're happy. There's always a reason to wait — that's the point of the excuse.

slides.title: Finding out is [[worse]]
slides.body: Many partners on Reddit say discovering p*rn hurt far more than being told would have. Being found out feels like betrayal. Telling her feels like trust.

slides.title: It's not about [[confessing]] everything
slides.body: You don't need every detail. You need the truth: you've struggled with p*rn and you're working on it.

slides.title: If you're [[ready]]
items: Pick a calm time — not after a fight.
Start with "I want to be honest with you."
Share your plan to quit p*rn.
Let her react — don't rush her to forgive.
